title: Eigen benchmark comparison result
description: One harness invocation's output: a PARTIAL contribution to a larger result store. A file covers one machine, one ISA target, one toolchain, one Eigen commit, and the arms that a single benchmark binary registered (always 'eigen', plus at most one reference library). Merging is by (provenance.machine_config_id, provenance.toolchain.isa_target, provenance.toolchain fingerprint, provenance.eigen.commit) with per-row keys (op, arm, scalar, shape, threads). Nothing in this file may be interpreted as covering a combination it does not list in 'scope'.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of THIS schema that the file was written against. Consumers reject a major version they do not know.

run_id.description: Identifier unique across all result files ever produced. Convention: <machine_config_id>-<isa_target>-<arm>-<eigen commit_short>-<UTC timestamp compacted>, e.g. 'm4pro-neon-accelerate-e2a2fda17-20260820T160111Z'.

partial.description: Always true. Recorded explicitly so no consumer can treat any single file as a complete dataset. Completeness is a property of a merge, never of a contribution.

measurements.description: One row per (op, arm, scalar, shape, threads) that produced a timing. Rows that did not produce a timing belong in 'not_measured', never here with a zero or null value.

not_measured.description: Explicit negative results. A combination inside 'scope' that appears in neither 'measurements' nor here is a harness bug; reduce.py reports it as reason 'unaccounted'.

provenance_gaps.description: Facts the schema requires that this platform could not supply, with the reason. The corresponding provenance field is null. Populating this array is mandatory whenever a nullable provenance field is null: a published number must be able to say what was not knowable, not merely omit it.

field.description: JSON Pointer into this document, e.g. '/provenance/cpu/frequency_governor'.

source_files.description: Raw Google Benchmark JSON files this result was distilled from, for audit. Paths are relative to the result file.

arm_key.description: Arm token as it appears in field 1 of a benchmark name: 'eigen', or a vendor key such as 'openblas', 'mkl', 'aocl', 'blis', 'nvpl', 'armpl', 'accelerate', 'netlib', 'eigenblas'.

op_key.description: BLAS/LAPACK mnemonic with the type prefix stripped, or an Eigen-only key, matching a key in ops.toml.

shape.description: Dimension name to value. Keys and their order must match the shape family's 'dims' in ops.toml; the order is carried separately in 'shape_dims' so no consumer has to rely on object key order.

stat.description: Summary of one measured quantity across repetitions. 'median' and 'mad' are the reported pair (see .agents/benchmarking.md: compare medians plus a dispersion measure, never the best run). 'mean'/'stddev' are retained for cross-checking and may be null for an aggregate-only contribution.

mad.description: Median absolute deviation, in the same units as 'median'. Zero when count == 1.

cv.description: Coefficient of variation, stddev/mean, unitless. Null when mean is null or zero.

count.description: Number of repetitions the summary was computed from.

name.description: Google Benchmark 'run_name' verbatim: the aggregate-suffix-free full name. This is the join key. See CONTRACTS.md section 1 for the grammar. Never the 'name' field of an aggregate row, which carries a '_mean'/'_median'/'_stddev'/'_cv' suffix.

shape_dims.description: Ordered dimension names, matching the shape family's 'dims'.

shape_group.description: Name of the ops.toml group this point came from, when known. Lets a renderer band a plot without re-deriving the grouping.

threads.description: Google Benchmark thread count for this row. 1 when the name carries no '/threads:' field.

repetitions.description: Repetitions actually completed for this row.

flops_per_iteration.description: Flop count of ONE benchmark iteration, from the ops.toml formula for this op, scalar and shape. Identical for both arms of a comparison by construction; that is what makes the arm-to-arm ratio meaningful even when 'flops_nominal' is true.

flops_nominal.description: Mirrors ops.<OP>.flops.nominal. True means the absolute rate is a convention, not a hardware-efficiency figure; renderers must label such columns.

samples.description: Per-repetition raw values, retained whenever the harness ran with --benchmark_report_aggregates_only=false (the default). Each array has 'repetitions' entries in repetition_index order. Absent for an aggregate-only contribution.

flop_rate.description: Flops per second, i.e. the raw value of the GFLOPS counter in the Google Benchmark JSON. It is NOT gigaflops: the kIs1000 argument in the counter idiom affects console rendering only.

source_time_unit.description: Time unit of the raw Google Benchmark rows ('ns', 'us', 'ms', 's'). Informational only: every time in this file is already in seconds.

validated.description: Whether the harness checked this arm's result against a reference computation outside the timed region. Null means the benchmark did not offer a check.

not_measured_entry.description: An explicit 'not measured'. This representation is preserved end to end: reduce.py keeps it, render.py prints the rendering token for the reason, plots.py leaves a gap in the series. It is never coerced to zero and never dropped.

scalar.description: Null means the entry covers every scalar in scope for this op.

shape.description: Null means the entry covers the whole grid for this op.

detail.description: Human-readable specifics, rendered in tooltips and in the coverage manifest. For reason 'no_reference_equivalent' this SHOULD be ops.<OP>.reference.reason verbatim.

scope.description: What this invocation ATTEMPTED. Consumers derive coverage as (scope cross product) minus (measurements) minus (not_measured). Without it, an absent row is indistinguishable from an unattempted one.

shape_groups.description: Per-op list of ops.toml group names attempted. An op absent from this object attempted its family's default_groups.

ops_toml_sha256.description: Digest of the ops.toml the scope was computed from, so a merge can detect grids that shifted under it.

provenance.description: Everything needed to reproduce and defend a published number years later. Sub-objects allow additional properties so a new machine fact does not invalidate old files; the top level and measurement rows do not, because those are the join surface.

timestamp_utc.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant the run started. Must carry the 'Z' suffix; local offsets are rejected. Note that Google Benchmark's context 'date' is local time and must be converted.

machine_config_id.description: Key of the benchmarks/comparison/machines/<id>.toml describing this host. The stable identity across runs; hostname is not, because hosts get renamed and cloud instances are ephemeral.

model.description: Vendor model string verbatim, e.g. 'Intel(R) Xeon(R) Platinum 8480+' or 'Apple M4 Pro'.

performance_cores.description: For heterogeneous CPUs (Apple silicon, Intel P/E). Null on homogeneous parts.

smt_enabled.description: Whether simultaneous multithreading was ON during the run. Null only where the platform genuinely does not expose it, with a provenance_gaps entry.

frequency_governor.description: Governor / power policy in force, e.g. 'performance', 'powersave', 'schedutil'. Null on platforms with no user-visible governor (macOS), with a provenance_gaps entry.

caches.description: Cache hierarchy. Google Benchmark's context 'caches' array maps directly onto this.

policy.description: Allocation policy in force, e.g. 'default', 'interleave=all', 'bind=0', or 'n/a' on a non-NUMA platform.

cpu_binding.description: Affinity actually applied to the benchmark process, e.g. 'taskset 0-31', 'numactl --cpunodebind=0', or null for none.

cxx_flags.description: The EXACT compile command flags, one token per element, as passed to the compiler for the benchmark translation unit. Not a summary and not a CMake variable name: a reader must be able to reconstruct the command.

isa_target.description: ISA target key, matching the ci/scripts naming: 'x86-64', 'x86-64-avx2', 'x86-64-avx512', 'aarch64-neon', 'aarch64-sve', 'aarch64-sme', 'ppc64le-vsx'. Free-form so a new target is data, not code.

benchmark_library_version.description: Google Benchmark version, from its JSON context 'library_version', e.g. 'v1.9.5'.

requested_threads.description: Thread count the run was configured for. 1 for a single-threaded comparison.

env.description: Thread-count and affinity environment variables ACTUALLY SET in the benchmark process, verbatim, name to value. Record only what was set; an absent variable is meaningfully different from one set to its default. At minimum probe OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, BLIS_NUM_THREADS, NVPL_BLAS_NUM_THREADS, ARMPL_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS, GOTO_NUM_THREADS, OMP_PROC_BIND, OMP_PLACES, KMP_AFFINITY, EIGEN_NB_THREADS.

eigen_nb_threads.description: Value returned by Eigen::nbThreads() in the benchmark process. Null when Eigen threading was not compiled in.

arms.description: Descriptor for every arm this file carries measurements or negative results for. MUST contain 'eigen'. A reference arm's library_version is mandatory: a rate without the library version it came from cannot be defended.

library_name.description: Display name, e.g. 'Eigen', 'OpenBLAS', 'Intel oneMKL', 'AOCL-BLIS', 'BLIS', 'NVPL BLAS', 'Arm Performance Libraries', 'Apple Accelerate', 'Netlib reference BLAS/LAPACK'.

library_version.description: Version string as the library itself reports it (openblas_get_config, mkl_get_version_string, bli_info_get_version_str, ARMPL_BUILD_STRING, or the packaged version when the library exposes no query). MANDATORY and never null: 'unknown' is only acceptable as the literal string with a matching provenance_gaps entry, because vendor releases change kernels without changing the API.

library_path.description: Resolved path of the shared object actually loaded, from the linker or the loader map. Distinguishes two builds reporting the same version.

interface.description: Integer width of the library interface: 'lp64' (32-bit int) or 'ilp64' (64-bit int).

commit.description: Full 40-character commit SHA of the Eigen checkout the benchmark was compiled against.

dirty.description: True when the worktree had uncommitted changes. A dirty result is not reproducible and renderers must mark it.

argv.description: run.py's own argv, one token per element, so the run can be repeated verbatim.

benchmark_argv.description: Flags passed to the benchmark executable.

repetitions.description: --benchmark_repetitions the run requested. Individual rows record what they actually completed.

memory_budget_bytes.description: Ceiling in bytes on one benchmark's operands, from the machine profile's [memory].benchmark_budget_bytes and enforced in the binary before it allocates. Null means no budget was enforced. A cell whose operands exceed it appears in not_measured with reason 'out_of_memory' rather than killing the process, which would lose every cell already measured in this invocation.

cpu_scaling_enabled.description: Google Benchmark's context 'cpu_scaling_enabled'. True means the frequency was not pinned and the numbers carry that caveat.

notes.description: Anything about the run that could not be controlled and must be disclosed.
